chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever says when dawn rises: "There is no god but Allah, Alone, no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He gives life and causes death, and He gives life and causes death, and He is Ever-Living and will not die. In His Hand is the good, and He is Able over all things," ten times; and sends blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad ten times; and glorifies (SubhanAllah) thirty-five times; and proclaims Oneness (La Ilaha Illa Allah) thirty-five times; and praises Allah (Alhamdulillah) thirty-five times, will not be written among the heedless that morning. And when he says it in the evening, he will not be written among the heedless that night.'

key_terms.بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ: In His Hand is the good
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah
key_terms.هَلَّلَ: proclaimed Oneness (said La Ilaha Illa Allah)
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: He gives life and causes death

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended morning and evening remembrance routine to avoid being among the heedless?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) prescribes this specific morning and evening dhikr routine, emphasizing the recitation of divine attributes alongside Salawat and the fourfold Tasbih (Tasbih, Tahlil, Tahmid, Takbir) to secure spiritual vigilance. This practice is rooted in the Shia tradition of maintaining constant awareness of God, ensuring the believer is not counted among the 'heedless' (al-ghafilin) who neglect their spiritual duties. The emphasis on morning and evening recitations aligns with the prophetic tradition of anchoring daily life in remembrance, a concept deeply explored in Shia tafsir and hadith literature.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ismail Bin Jabir, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘The one who says when the dawn emerges, ‘There is no god except Allahazwj, Alone, there being no associate for Himazwj. For Himazwj is the Kingdom and for Himazwj is the Praise. Heazwj Causes to live and Heazwj Causes to die, and Heazwj Causes to die and Heazwj Causes to live, and Heazwj is Living and will not be dying. In Hisazwj Hand is the goodness, and Heazwj is Able upon everything’, ten times’ And send Salawāts upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww ten times, and Glorify (Subhan-Allahazwj) thirty five times, and Extol the Oneness (La Ilaha Illa Allahazwj) thirty five times, and Praise Allahazwj (Al Hamd Lil Allahazwj) thirty five times, would not be Written during that morning as being from the neglectful ones. And when he says it during the evening, he would not be Written during that night as being from the neglectful ones’.
en.sarwar: 35. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Isma’Il ibn Jabir from ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘Whoever says before dawn, “No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah alone, Who has no partner, to Him belongs the kingdom and all praise, He gives life, causes death, causes death and gives life. He is living and does not die, in His hand is all good and He has power over all things,” ten times and says, ‘O Lord, grant al-Salat (favors) upon Muhammad and his family,’ ten times, and says, ‘Allah is free of all defects,’ thirty-five times, ‘No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah,’ thirty- five times, ‘All praise belongs to Allah,’ thirty-five times, he will not be written that morning among the careless ones and if he says this in the evening, he will not be written of the careless ones in that night.’”
